He was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with the sixth overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. Giddey is the youngest player in NBA history to record a [[triple-double]], having done so at 19 years, 84 days old. He also became the first rookie since Hall of Famer [[Oscar Robertson]] in 1961 to record three consecutive triple-doubles.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=De Silva|title=Josh Giddey becomes first NBA rookie since 1961 to record three consecutive triple-doubles|url=https://wwos.nine.com.au/basketball/nba-news-josh-giddey-triple-double-streak-continues/a2410ce9-4a2c-40b0-995c-9e8ccb7e6c62|website=WWOS.nine.com.au|date=17 February 2022|access-date=27 February 2022}} ==Early life and career== Giddey was born on October 10, 2002, in [[Melbourne, Victoria]], Australia, to professional basketball players Kim and [[Warrick Giddey]].{{cite news|first=Tom|last=Maddocks|title=Josh Giddey, Australian basketball's next big thing, is set to jump from the NBL to the NBA|date=14 March 2021|work=ABC News|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-03-14/josh-giddey-could-be-australian-basketballs-next-big-thing/13243664|access-date=29 November 2023}} Warrick made the Australian Schoolboys teams in both [[Rugby league]] and [[Rugby union]] before playing for the [[Illawarra Hawks]] and [[Melbourne Tigers]] in the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL), while Kim played for the Melbourne Tigers women’s basketball team in the [[Women's National Basketball League]] (WNBL).{{Cite news |last=Snape |first=Jack |date=2025-11-22 |title=‘He’s the real thing’: Longley feels Chicago connection as Josh Giddey brings Bulls back to the big time |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/nov/23/nba-basketball-chicago-bulls-josh-giddey-luc-longley-australia-connection |access-date=2025-11-23 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{cite web |last=Ward |first=Roy |title=NBA prospect Giddey learns big lessons in NBL |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/nba-prospect-giddey-learns-big-lessons-in-nbl-20210114-p56u38.html |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=21 May 2021 |date=16 January 2021}} Giddey grew up supporting [[Hawthorn Football Club]]{{Cite web |date=2022-11-07 |title=Sliding doors moment that changed Josh Giddey’s life: ‘I was better at footy’ |url=https://7news.com.au/sport/basketball/the-sliding-doors-moment-that-changed-josh-giddeys-career-path-forever-i-was-better-at-footy-c-8784516 |access-date=2025-12-05 |website=7NEWS |language=en}} whilst living in [[Yarraville, Victoria|Yarraville]] and attended [[St Kevin's College, Melbourne|St Kevin's College]] in [[Toorak]] from Years 7 to 10, before emerging as one of Australia's top basketball prospects with the [[NBA Global Academy]], a training center part of the [[BA Centre of Excellence]] at the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] (AIS) in [[Canberra]].{{cite web |last=Makeham |first=Jake |title=Australian Giddey to achieve NBA dream with Oklahoma City Thunder |url=https://www.mojonews.com.au/josh-giddey-the-latest-australian-to-achieve-their-nba-dream?amp=1 |website=Mojo News |access-date=8 August 2021 |date=30 July 2021}}{{cite web |last=Uluc |first=Olgun |title=Josh Giddey emerges out of nowhere to become one of Australia's elite prospects |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/josh-giddey-emerges-out-of-nowhere-to-become-one-of-australias-elite-prospects/news-story/321762fc60789f6eca8f8d7da9eb6270 |work=[[Fox Sports (Australian TV network)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=18 July 2019}} He attended [[UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra]] alongside his full-time training at the AIS.{{cite web |title=August 2021 Newsletter |url=https://www.lakeonline.act.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0008/523439/Issue_5_LAKENEWS_August.pdf |website=UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra |access-date=15 November 2021 |date=August 2021}} [[File:Josh Giddey (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Giddey with the NBA Global Academy in 2020]] At the Australian Under-18 Championships in April 2019, Giddey averaged 20 points, 8.3 rebounds and six assists per game, leading VIC Metro to the title.{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey: The road so far for Melbourne's next great prospect |url=https://pickandroll.com.au/josh-giddey-the-road-ahead-for-melbournes-next-great-prospect/ |publisher=The Pick and Roll |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=3 October 2019}} In January 2020, Giddey helped the NBA Global Academy win the Torneo Junior Ciutat de L'Hospitalet in [[Barcelona]], where he earned [[most valuable player]] (MVP) honors.{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey named MVP as the NBA Global Academy Triumphs at the 2020 Torneo Junio Ciutat de L'Hospitalet |url=https://australia.basketball/blog/2020/01/15/josh-giddey-named-mvp-as-the-nba-global-academy-triumphs-at-the-2020-torneo-junio-ciutat-de-lhospitalet/ |publisher=[[Basketball Australia]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=15 January 2020 |archive-date=5 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505235633/https://australia.basketball/blog/2020/01/15/josh-giddey-named-mvp-as-the-nba-global-academy-triumphs-at-the-2020-torneo-junio-ciutat-de-lhospitalet/ |url-status=dead }} In the following month at [[2020 NBA All-Star Game#All-Star Weekend|NBA All-Star Weekend]] in [[Chicago]], he took part in [[Basketball Without Borders]] and was named an all-star of the camp.{{cite web |last=Kidane |first=Benyam |title=Fresh off being named a Basketball Without Borders All-Star and being selected for the Australian Boomers, Josh Giddey continues to make waves |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nba/news/basketball-without-borders-all-star-australian-boomers-josh-giddey-nba-academy/b06khrg3q6xh1cfu5gjrsdql2 |website=[[Sporting News]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=18 February 2020}} {{clear left}} ==Professional career== ===Adelaide 36ers (2020–2021)=== On 12 March 2020, Giddey signed with the [[Adelaide 36ers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) as a part of the league's [[NBL Next Stars Program|Next Stars program]] to develop [[NBA draft]] prospects, and he became the first Australian player to be a part of the program.{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey to Become NBL Next Star with Adelaide 36ers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/josh-giddey-to-become-nbl-next-star-with-adelaide-36ers |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=12 March 2020 |archive-date=10 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410131943/https://nbl.com.au/news/josh-giddey-to-become-nbl-next-star-with-adelaide-36ers |url-status=dead }} Giddey turned down offers from several [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].{{cite web |last=Uluc |first=Olgun |title=Josh Giddey, a 2021 point guard out of the NBA Global Academy picks up offer from Arizona - sources |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/josh-giddey-a-2021-point-guard-out-of-the-nba-global-academy-picks-up-offer-from-arizona-sources/news-story/28fd6e08b74baf841eac33b105914267 |work=[[Fox Sports (Australian TV network)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=26 August 2019}} On 26 April 2021, he recorded 12 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 93–77 loss to the [[New Zealand Breakers]],{{cite web |title=Breakers vs 36ers |url=https://www.fibalivestats.com/u/NBL/1869890/bs.html |work=FIBALiveStats.com |access-date=26 April 2021 |date=26 April 2021}} becoming the youngest Australian in NBL history to record a [[triple-double]].{{cite web |date=26 April 2021 |title=Youngest Australian in NBL history to record a triple double |url=https://x.com/NBL/status/1386642755590311940 |access-date=26 April 2021 |work=x.com/NBL}} In the 36ers' next game against the [[Brisbane Bullets]] on 1 May, he became the first ever Australian to record a triple-double in consecutive games, finishing with 15 points, 13 assists and 11 rebounds in a 101–79 win.{{cite web |title=Night of Sixers celebrations against Bullets |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/night-of-sixers-celebrations-against-bullets |work=NBL.com.au |access-date=1 May 2021 |date=1 May 2021}} He had a third triple-double on 9 May in a 97–88 overtime win over the [[Sydney Kings]], finishing with 11 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds.{{cite web |title=DJ delivers in OT as Giddey racks up another triple-double |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/dj-delivers-in-ot-as-giddey-racks-up-another-triple-double |work=NBL.com.au |access-date=9 May 2021 |date=9 May 2021}} Giddey was released from the active playing roster on 17 May to prepare for the [[2021 NBA draft]], and finished the season averaging 10.9 points, 7.3 rebounds and a league-leading 7.6 assists per game in 28 games played.{{cite web |title=Josh Giddey released from Adelaide 36ers active playing roster as Club supports his next step |url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/josh-giddey-released-from-adelaide-36ers-active-playing-roster-as-club-supports-his-next-step |website=Adelaide 36ers |access-date=17 May 2021 |date=17 May 2021}}{{cite web |last=Uluc |first=Olgun |date=17 May 2021 |title=Josh Giddey released from 36ers' playing roster as he prepares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/31458608 |access-date=17 May 2021 |website=ESPN}} He was selected as the [[NBL Rookie of the Year]].{{cite web |title=Bryce Cotton Claims Third Andrew Gaze MVP Trophy |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bryce-cotton-claims-third-andrew-gaze-mvp-trophy |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=30 June 2021 |date=16 June 2021}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2021–2024)=== ====2021-22 season==== On 27 April 2021, Giddey declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], where he was projected to be a [[lottery pick]].{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=27 April 2021 |title=Aussie playmaking guard Giddey to enter draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31347794 |access-date=28 April 2021 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On 29 July, he was drafted as the sixth overall pick by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], and on 8 August, Giddey signed a contract with the Thunder.{{cite web |title=Thunder Signs First-Round Draft Picks Josh Giddey and Tre Mann |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/release/giddey-mann-210808 |website=NBA.com |access-date=15 August 2021 |date=8 August 2021}} That same day, he suffered an ankle injury five minutes into his [[NBA Summer League]] debut and was ruled out for the rest of the competition as a precautionary measure.{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |title=Josh Giddey to miss Thunder summer league finale with ankle injury |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/08/16/josh-giddey-thunder-summer-league-finale-ankle-injury/ |website=USA Today |access-date=18 August 2021 |date=16 August 2021}} On 20 October, Giddey made his NBA debut, putting up four points, 10 rebounds and three assists in a 107–86 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |date=20 October 2021 |title=Josh Giddey impresses in NBA debut but Jazz win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32442964 |access-date=20 October 2021 |website=ESPN.com |agency=AAP}} On 27 October, Giddey recorded his first double-double with 18 points and 10 assists in a 123–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], while also becoming the third-youngest player to record at least 10 assists in a game, behind only [[LeBron James]], who did so twice.{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-10-28/josh-giddey-history-double-double-oklahoma-city-win-lakers/100576852|title=Josh Giddey makes history with double-double as Oklahoma City beat Los Angeles Lakers|website=ABC News|date=27 October 2021|access-date=27 November 2021}} Giddey was named the NBA Western Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in October/November.{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2021 |title=Josh Giddey, Evan Mobley named NBA Rookies of the Month |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-rookies-of-month-josh-giddey-evan-mobley |access-date=21 December 2021 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On 26 December 2021, Giddey became the second player in NBA history, after [[Norm Van Lier]], to record a scoreless double-double, as he compiled ten assists and ten rebounds in the Thunder's 117–112 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web |last=Quinn |first=Sam |date=27 December 2021 |title=Thunder's Josh Giddey posts scoreless double-double, becoming second NBA player in history to do so |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/thunders-josh-giddey-posts-scoreless-double-double-becoming-second-nba-player-in-history-to-do-so/ |access-date=30 November 2024 |website=cbssports.com}} Giddey was named the NBA Western Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in December.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-rookies-month-december-josh-giddey-franz-wagner|title=Franz Wagner, Josh Giddey named NBA Rookies of the Month|website=NBA.com|date=4 January 2022|access-date=4 February 2022}} On 2 January 2022, Giddey became the youngest-ever player to record a triple-double, with 17 points, 14 assists and 13 rebounds in a 95–86 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]], surpassing the previous record set by [[LaMelo Ball]].{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/josh-giddey-grabs-youngest-triple-double-in-nba-history-in-loss-to-dallas|title=Josh Giddey Grabs Youngest Triple-Double in NBA History in Loss to Dallas|magazine=Sports Illustrated|last=Lovelace|first=Ross|date=2 January 2022|access-date=2 January 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/thunder-news-josh-giddey-steals-lamelo-ball-thunder-via-epic-new-record/|title=Thunder rookie Josh Giddey steals LaMelo Ball's thunder via epic new record|website=ClutchPoints|last=Samillano|first=Gerard|date=2 January 2022|access-date=2 January 2022}} Giddey was named the NBA Western Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in January and again in February, winning the award four consecutive times.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-rookies-month-january-cade-cunningham-josh-giddey|title=Cade Cunningham, Josh Giddey named NBA Rookies of the Month|website=NBA.com|date=2 February 2022|access-date=4 February 2022}}{{cite web|url= https://www.nba.com/news/scottie-barnes-josh-giddey-named-nba-rookies-of-the-month-for-february?amp=1|title=Scottie Barnes, Josh Giddey named NBA Rookies of the Month for February|website=NBA.com|date=3 March 2022|access-date=8 April 2022}} On 27 March, Giddey was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to hip soreness,{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Andrew |date=27 March 2022 |title=Josh Giddey's unbelievable rookie season over after 'unpredictable' injury |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/nba-2022-josh-giddey-injury-update-out-for-season-hip-soreness-oklahoma-city-thunder-rookie-of-the-year-records/news-story/9660fb9b6be5a5cfd6a9a11557936cc9 |access-date=26 March 2022 |website=Fox Sports}} and finished the season averaging 12.5 points, 7.8 rebounds and 6.4 assists per game while shooting .419, .263 and .709 from the field, the three-point line and on free throws, respectively, with four triple-doubles. In addition, he was the sole rookie to tally at least 500 points, 400 rebounds and 300 assists.{{cite web|last=Buckley|first=Zach|date=14 April 2022|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2955308-grading-every-2022-nba-teams-rookie-class|title=Grading Every 2022 NBA Team's Rookie Class|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=15 April 2022}} ====2023-24 season==== On 10 January 2023, in a game against the [[Miami Heat]], Giddey joined [[Luka Dončić]], [[Ben Simmons]] and [[Grant Hill]] as the only players in NBA history to record at least 1,000 points, 700 rebounds and 500 assists in their first 100 career games.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/thunder-news-josh-giddey-joins-luka-doncic-exclusive-list-incredible-feat|title=Thunder star Josh Giddey joins Luka Doncic on exclusive list with incredible feat|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=10 January 2023|access-date=10 January 2023}} On 15 January, Giddey scored a season-high 28 points along with nine rebounds and assists, leading Oklahoma City to a 112–102 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |date=2023-01-16 |title='This is incredible': Giddey's brutal act as Aussie 'looks like an All-Star' in career-best showing |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/nba-2023-josh-giddey-okc-thunder-v-brooklyn-nets-ben-simmons-back-injury-golden-state-warriors-road-problems-loss-to-chicago-bulls-scores-results-updates-latest-highlights-video/news-story/c7ca086927e3c929aa53104d7115bbec |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=Fox Sports |language=en}} On 12 April, during the [[NBA play-in tournament]], Giddey recorded 31 points, 10 assists and nine rebounds in a 123–118 win over the New Orleans Pelicans, advancing the Thunder to the eighth-seed game.{{cite web |title=Gilgeous-Alexander leads Thunder past Pelicans in play-in |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap/_/gameId/401539674 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=13 April 2023 |date=12 April 2023 }} On 11 January 2024, Giddey logged 13 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists in 22 minutes against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. In doing so, he became the first player in NBA history to post a triple-double on 100% field-goal accuracy in under 25 minutes.{{cite web|title='First in history': Giddey's trade statement in epic triple double as 'NFL' play rocks NBA|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/nba-2024-josh-giddey-records-one-of-fastest-triple-doubles-of-all-time-against-portland-trailblazers-scores-video-reaction/news-story/bff0feb4eeb7c8ca09c11fae36d5c2b4|website=FOXSports.com|date=12 January 2024|access-date=3 March 2024}} ===Chicago Bulls (2024–present)=== ====2024–25 season==== On 21 June 2024, Giddey was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for guard [[Alex Caruso]].{{cite web|title=Chicago Bulls acquire Josh Giddey in trade with Oklahoma City Thunder|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-josh-giddey-in-trade-with-oklahoma-city-thunder|website=NBA.com|date=21 June 2024|access-date=21 June 2024}} On 2 December, Giddey put up a triple-double with 20 points, 13 rebounds and 11 assists in a 128–102 win over the [[2024–25 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Sam |author-link=Sam Smith (sportswriter) |date=December 3, 2024 |title=Josh Giddey's triple-double leads Bulls over Nets, Matas Buzelis shines |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/josh-giddeys-triple-double-leads-bulls-over-nets-matas-buzelis-shines |access-date=December 29, 2024 |website=nba.com}} On 28 December, he put up a triple-double with 23 points, 15 rebounds and 10 assists in a 116–111 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He also became the first player in Bulls franchise history since [[Jimmy Butler]] to record multiple games with triple-doubles in a season.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/bulls-news-josh-giddey-mvp-praise-from-doc-rivers-heroic-triple-double|title=Bulls' Josh Giddey earns 'MVP' praise from Doc Rivers after heroic triple-double|website=ClutchPoints|last=Brown|first=Malik|date=December 29, 2024|access-date=December 29, 2024}} On 8 March, he recorded his third triple-double of the season with 26 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds in a 114–109 victory against the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-pull-off-17-point-comeback-win-over-miami-giddey-records-third-triple-double-as-a-bull|title=Bulls pull off 17-point comeback win over Miami, Giddey records third triple-double as a Bull|website=nba.com|last=Smith|first=Sam|date=March 8, 2025|access-date=March 9, 2025}} On 22 March, Giddey recorded a near [[quadruple-double]] (the last quadruple-double was achieved in 1994) with 15 points, 17 assists, 10 rebounds, and a career-high eight steals in a 146–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |date=23 March 2025 |title=LeBron James' return from injury spoiled by Bulls' phenomenal effort in 146-115 win over Lakers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705594 |access-date=23 March 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Sam |title=Bulls dominate Lakers behind Josh Giddey's historic stat line, 146-115 {{!}} Chicago Bulls |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-dominate-lakers-behind-josh-giddeys-historic-stat-line-146-115 |access-date=24 March 2025 |work=www.nba.com |date=23 March 2025 |language=en}}{{cite news |title=Giddey leaves his mark in LA with triple-double |url=https://au.news.yahoo.com/giddey-leaves-mark-la-triple-052430010.html |access-date=24 March 2025 |work=Yahoo News |date=23 March 2025 |language=en-AU}} On 27 March, Giddey put up a triple-double with 25 points, 14 rebounds, 11 assists, and hit a buzzer-beating game-winner from half court in a 119–117 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.{{cite web |title=Giddey's 47-foot buzzer-beater lifts red-hot Bulls to wild win over Lakers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44437104/giddey-47-foot-buzzer-beater-lifts-red-hot-bulls-wild-win-lakers |website=ESPN.com |access-date=27 March 2025 |date=27 March 2025}} This was Giddey's 5th triple-double of the season and he joined [[Michael Jordan]] as the only Bulls in franchise history to have 5+ triple-doubles in a single season.{{Citeweb|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/chicago-bulls/news/josh-giddey-shares-record-michael-jordan/5e48f61450629e21b12b7568|title=Josh Giddey shares incredible Bulls record with Michael Jordan|last=Bishop|first=Drew|publisher=[[Sporting News]]|access-date=27 March 2025 |date=27 March 2025}} On 9 April, in a 119-111 win over the [[Miami Heat]], Giddey had 28 points, 16 rebounds and 11 assists while tallying his 7th triple-double of the season. Giddey also joined Michael Jordan and [[Scottie Pippen]] as the only Bulls players to have seasons with at least 1,000 points, 500 rebounds, and 500 assists.{{Citeweb|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/josh_giddey_joins_franchise_legends_in_first_season_with_bulls/s1_13132_42030590|title=Josh Giddey joins franchise legends in first season with Bulls|last=Mohan|first=Sai|publisher=[[Yardbarker]]|date=10 April 2025|accessdate=10 April 2025}} ====2025–26 season==== On 9 September 2025, Giddey re-signed with the Bulls on a four-year, $100 million contract.{{cite web|title=Josh Giddey agrees to 4-year, $100M extension with Bulls|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46208674/josh-giddey-agrees-4-year-100m-extension-bulls|website=ESPN.com|date=9 September 2025|access-date=9 September 2025}} On 31 October, Giddey scored a career-high 32 points along with 10 rebounds and nine assists in a 135–125 win over the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]], leading the Bulls to their first 5–0 start since the [[1996–97 Chicago Bulls season|1996–97 season]].{{cite web|title=Josh Giddey scores 32 for undefeated Bulls in win vs. Knicks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46798355/josh-giddey-scores-32-undefeated-bulls-win-vs-knicks|website=ESPN.com|date=1 November 2025|access-date=1 November 2025}} On 4 November, Giddey put up a triple-double with 29 points, 15 rebounds, and 12 assists in a 113–111 win over the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]]. It was his second consecutive game with a triple-double, allowing Giddey to become the first player since [[Michael Jordan]] in 1989 to record a triple-double in consecutive games in Bulls franchise history.{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/nba/chicago-bulls/bulls-news-josh-giddey-pulls-off-eye-popping-feat-last-done-by-1988-89-michael-jordan|title= Bulls’ Josh Giddey pulls off eye-popping feat last done by 1988-89 Michael Jordan|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=November 4, 2025|access-date=November 5, 2025}}{{cite web|url= https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/rare-air-big-money-pressure-no-concern-as-josh-giddey-joins-michael-jordan-in-bulls-record-books-20251105-p5n7zd.html|title= Rare air: Big-money pressure no concern as Josh Giddey joins Michael Jordan in Bulls record books|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|last=Ward|first=Roy|date=November 5, 2025|access-date=November 5, 2025}} On 17 December, Giddey put up a triple-double with 23 points, 11 rebounds, 11 assists, and a career-high-tying five three-pointers made in a 127–111 win over the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He joined [[Michael Jordan]] as the only players to put up at least 10 triple-doubles in Bulls franchise history and also became the first player to put up a triple-double with at least five three-pointers made in Bulls franchise history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/chicago-bulls/bulls-news-josh-giddeys-stat-line-cavaliers-michael-jordan-club|title=Bulls star Josh Giddey’s wild stat line vs. Cavaliers puts him in Michael Jordan club|website=ClutchPoints|last=Imran|first=Abdullah|date=December 18, 2025|access-date=December 18, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/nba-2025-josh-giddey-chicago-bulls-win-over-cleveland-cavaliers-tripledouble-scores-results-highlights-latest-news-jock-landale-memphis-grizzlies-win-over-minnesota-timberwolves/news-story/72842d4bed105b8d02509e212334ade3|title=Giddey joins greats with All-Star statement; clutch hero delivers dual Aussie eruption — NBA Wrap|website=Fox Sports Australia|last=Cotton|first=Ben|date=December 18, 2025|access-date=December 18, 2025}} Giddey made 54 total appearances (including 51 starts) for the Bulls during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 17.0 points, 8.3 rebounds, and 9.1 assists (all of which were career-highs). On May 13, 2026, it was announced that Giddey had undergone [[arthroscopy|arthroscopic]] surgery to repair a right ankle injury.{{Cite web|title=Bulls guard Josh Giddey (ankle) undergoes arthroscopic surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/news/josh-giddey-arthroscopic-surgery|access-date=May 28, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== Giddey represented [[Australia national under-17 basketball team|Australia]] at the 2019 [[FIBA]] Under-17 Oceania Championship in [[New Caledonia]]. He averaged 16.4 points, 7.4 rebounds and five assists per game and was named to the All-Star Five after leading his team to a gold medal. In the final against [[New Zealand]], he collected 25 points, eight rebounds, six assists and five steals in an 85–56 win.{{cite web |title=FIBA U17 Oceania Championship All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/oceania/u17/2019/news/fiba-u17-oceania-championship-all-star-five |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=1 April 2020 |date=25 August 2019}} ===Senior national team=== On 23 February 2020, Giddey made his debut for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australia national basketball team]] during [[2021 FIBA Asia Cup qualification]]. He recorded 11 points, six assists and three rebounds in 11 minutes, helping Australia defeat [[Hong Kong basketball team|Hong Kong]], 115–52.{{cite web |date=23 February 2020 |title=Teen Giddey shines on debut in huge Boomers win |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/giddey-debuts-in-huge-boomers-win-20200223-p543jf.html |access-date=1 April 2020 |website=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]] |agency=AAP}} Giddey became the youngest player to play for the senior team since [[Ben Simmons]] in 2013.{{cite web |date=20 February 2020 |title=Kings' Bogut delivers rocket to NBL admin |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/28928239 |access-date=1 April 2020 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=AAP}} Giddey was one of the final cuts from the Australian basketball team roster for the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Tokyo Olympics]] and was instead selected as one of three emergency players.{{cite web |last=Wenzel |first=Murray |title=Giddey misses cut as Boomers chase gold |url=https://7news.com.au/sport/basketball/giddey-misses-cut-as-boomers-chase-gold-c-3297938 |website=7 News |access-date=3 July 2021 |date=3 July 2021}} Giddey represented Australia in the [[2023 FIBA World Cup]] and averaged 19.4 points, 5 rebounds and 6 assists.
